### Describe the bug

When running `gh actions` with an unknown subcommand, such as `gh actions list`, `gh actions run`, etc., the output doesn't have a newline at the end.

### Affected version

gh version 2.46.0 (2025-12-13 Ubuntu 2.46.0-4)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.46.0

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Type this 'gh actions list'
2. View the output at the end
3. See error

### Expected vs actual behavior

A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen and what actually happened.

Expected:
```
...
gh actions [flags]
$
```
Actual:
```
...
gh actions [flags]$
```

### Logs

```
someone@someones-desktop:~/somerepo$ gh actions list
unknown command "list" for "gh actions"

Usage:  gh actions [flags]someone@someones-desktop:~/somerepo$ 
```

<!-- Note: Set `GH_DEBUG=true` for verbose logs or `GH_DEBUG=api` for verbose logs with HTTP traffic details. -->
title: gh actions unknown subcommand output doesn't end with a newline

### Describe the bug

For a namespaced skill, `gh skill` installs a flat directory but records the namespaced name in the shared `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. The Vercel `skills` CLI then treats that lock entry as missing and fails to update it.

### Affected versions

- GitHub CLI `2.105.0`
- `skills` CLI `1.9.0`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a GitHub-hosted namespaced skill with `gh skill install`, using user scope.
2. Compare its flat installed directory name with its namespaced entry in `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`.
3. Run `skills update --global`.

### Expected vs actual behavior

The shared lock entry should be compatible with the installed directory and the `skills` updater. Instead, the updater reports the namespaced entry as missing and fails with `No matching skills found`.

### Investigation

The installer [records `skill.InstallName()`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.105.0/internal/skills/installer/installer.go#L79), which includes the namespace, but [installs using the flat `skill.Name`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.105.0/internal/skills/installer/installer.go#L250-L254). The lock file is intended for [Vercel CLI interoperability](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.105.0/internal/skills/lockfile/lockfile.go#L17).

Removing the duplicate namespaced lock entries while retaining the unprefixed entries and installed files restored `skills update --global`. Future `gh skill` installs or updates may recreate them.
title: gh skill writes namespaced lock keys for flat installations, breaking skills update

body:
### Describe the bug

When an environment-provided classic token lacks a scope, `gh api` suggests `gh auth refresh`. The suggested command fails because `gh` cannot update an environment-provided token. I reproduced this with `gh` 2.105.0 and 2.102.0 on Linux using an isolated loopback API and a synthetic token.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an isolated shell, export a classic personal access token that has `repo` and lacks both `user` and `user:email` as `GH_TOKEN`.
2. Run `gh api --hostname github.com user/emails`.
3. Run the command printed in the scope hint.

The same diagnostic path can be reproduced without a real token or account. Configure `GH_HOST=127.0.0.1` and a dummy `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` with a temporary `GH_CONFIG_DIR`. Serve HTTPS locally for `GET /api/v3/user/emails` and return HTTP 404 with `{"message":"Not Found"}`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-OAuth-Scopes: repo`, and `X-Accepted-OAuth-Scopes: user, user:email`. Trust the local certificate for the experiment and run the two commands below.

```text
$ gh api --hostname 127.0.0.1 user/emails
{"message":"Not Found"}
gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)
gh: This API operation needs the "user" scope. To request it, run:  gh auth refresh -h 127.0.0.1 -s user

$ gh auth refresh -h 127.0.0.1 -s user
The value of the GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN environment variable is being used for authentication.
To refresh credentials stored in GitHub CLI, first clear the value from the environment.
```

Both commands exit 1. The [email API documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/users/emails#list-email-addresses-for-the-authenticated-user) describes `user:email` as sufficient for classic tokens.

### Expected behavior and proposed change

Keep the missing-scope information and tailor the next step to the active credential. For an environment token, name the environment variable and suggest replacing its value with a credential that has the required permission. Suggest `gh auth refresh` for eligible stored credentials.

In [the API command's error handling](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.105.0/pkg/cmd/api/api.go#L560-L571), resolve the token source for the request host using the same authentication configuration as the API transport. Pass the source into the scope hint formatter, or pass back the missing scope and choose the remediation at the call site. [The refresh command](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.105.0/pkg/cmd/auth/refresh/refresh.go#L191-L195) already distinguishes environment-provided tokens. Test the same 404 response with a stored token and an environment-provided token and assert the appropriate hint for each.

### Workaround

Replace the exported token with a classic token that has `user:email` or a fine-grained user token with **Email addresses: Read**. To use stored credentials instead, clear the applicable environment token and sign in with `gh auth login -h github.com -s user:email --web`.

This is a concrete example of credential-specific remediation under [the actionable errors design](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/14038). It was investigated while working on [gh-setup-git-identity issue 34](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-setup-git-identity/issues/34).

[Runnable loopback reproduction](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-setup-git-identity/blob/03226cf54948b8e309d276bc53d2e312d3f57fe4/experiments/issue-34-gh-scope-hint.mjs)
title: gh api suggests auth refresh for missing scopes on an environment token
